SELF PORTRAIT IN WAR TIME . COMPLETED 2018 BY AMERICAN ARTIST PHIL KAYE. Here we see a gure in the foreground, intended to be the artist himself. The small gures at the bottom of the frame are thought to be heads, perhaps an audience or contemporaries in some sort of gathering. The scene evokes a dreamlike sequence, with a background consisting of a brick wall – an outside material, brought inside – perhaps a signi er of the artist blurring the line between reality and ction. The war to which the title alludes is unclear. Though historically speaking, it would be accurate to say that the piece was created during a time of war. Being of both Japanese and American descent, the artist had several members directly involved in war e orts in the 20th century, and thus the con icts at the time of the creation of the work could have particular resonance. 74. SELF PORTRAIT IN WAR TIME. COMPLETED 2018 BY AMERICAN ARTIST PHIL KAYE. Here we see a gure in the foreground, intended to be the artist himself. The artist often returned to self-portraiture, perhaps a re ection of an acute self-obsession, or perhaps a self-obsession pervasive throughout the art form. Or, perhaps, a self-obsession pervasive throughout the particular time period. The scene evokes a nightmarish sequence. The small gures at the bottom of the frame are thought to be heads or gods, invoking a sort of judgment ritual upon the artist. The nightmarish quality is furthered by the background consisting of a brick wall – a seemingly oating fortress, o ering no protection, and no escape. The war to which the title alludes is unclear. Though historically speaking, it would be accurate to say that the piece was created during a time of war – both domestically and abroad. While the artist frequently discussed both con icts, he was, in truth, largely una ected, enjoying stability, safety and relative prosperity. In fact, it could be argued that this portrait, depicting the artist only speaking of war, exempli es his lack of concrete connection with the con ict at all. 74. SELF PORTRAIT IN WAR TIME.
